run.description: Add the source a file declares, or replace the one of its name
does: it replaces one source and copies no command files, and changes nothing else. It grants no call, makes no hook, and sets no credential's file: the source keeps its env_file, mint_command, base or host, call limits and ignored senders, and every grant of it stands, now for this declaration.
source empty: its calls go to https://example.invalid. It names no credential.
it would replace the source empty the yard has under that name.
call health (read): GET /health. It takes no parameter, and sends no query.
call health sends no body. Its answer is returned as it comes, at most 65536 bytes.

it has no check call, no idempotency header, no way to tell a user, no way to hear deliveries, no limits command, no way to speak in threads, no bead link, no identity fold (its identity keys keep their case), no hook deliveries into the yard and no pull-request or CI events.
run.back: yardr bead ask <bead> - with Q: <question> and R: source add <a file holding the declaration that stands now> on stdin

carried.name: empty
carried.text:
name: empty
base: https://example.invalid
calls:
  health:
    kind: read
    request: {method: GET, path: /health}

weight.line: brings a program the yard will run: the declaration of empty replaces the one that stands, and says where the credential it keeps is sent and which programs the yard runs
